chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdul Kareem bin Amr, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'O Prophet! Surely We have made lawful for you your wives' — how many women were permissible for him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever he desired from anything.'

I said, 'And a believing woman if she gave herself to the Prophet.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The gifting is not permissible except for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and as for the others than the Messenger of Allah, marriage is not correct except with a dowry.'

I said, 'What is your view of the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'It is not permissible for you to take women afterwards'? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, it means by it, 'It is not permissible for you the women which Allah had prohibited in this Verse: 'Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters and your sisters and your paternal aunts and your maternal aunts' — up to the end of it.'

And had the matter been as you are saying, it would have been permissible for you what was not permissible for him, because one of you changes [wives] whenever he wants, but the matter is not as they are saying.

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, permitted for His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he marry from the women whatever he wanted, except what was prohibited to him in this Verse, in the Surah Al-Nisa.

key_terms.أَحْلَلْنَا لَكَ: We have made lawful for you
key_terms.الْهِبَةُ: The gift/gifting (of a woman in marriage)

ai.seo_question: What were the unique marital privileges of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) compared to the general Muslim community?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the unique marital privileges (Khasa'is) of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), distinguishing his unlimited capacity to marry and accept 'gifts' of women without a dowry from the general community's requirement of a formal contract and mahr. It specifically addresses the theological debate regarding the phrase 'la yahillu laka al-nisa' (it is not permissible for you to [marry] women), clarifying that this restriction refers only to the specific women made unlawful in Surah An-Nisa (kinship), rather than a general prohibition on all women as some opponents claimed. This distinction underscores the principle that the Prophet's permissions were exclusive and not automatically extended to the Ummah.
